To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the critical current of the conductor has been successfully measured up to 6.2T, that the conductor has a good performance and is ready to be used in the CMS magnet, that a critical current degradation has been detected in the conductor samples, that the critical current degradation is not uniform in the cross section of the conductor, that the degradation is more evident in the inner layers of the conductor and that the degradation is not correlated with the copper content of the conductor.

the critical current of the CMS conductor is stable and reproducible in fields up to at least 4.5 T, and that the critical current is higher than 10,000 A at 4 T and 4.2 K. The main takeaway from our work is that

the critical current measurements performed at the CMS test facility at INFM-Genova, using a different procedure from that adopted at the LHC, give a good agreement with the results obtained at the LHC.
the critical current of the CMS conductor is stable in time and in the presence of a magnetic field.
